target_customer: iPhone users with large email accounts who wanted full text search; IMAP and Rackspace accounts were premium features
problem: The iPhone Mail app of 2009 could not search message bodies quickly or offline, so users could not find old email.
business_model: Paid iPhone app with premium account types (consumer app sales)

founders.name: Gabor Cselle
founders.background_notes: YC page: after reMail spent about 2.5 years at Google on Gmail and Android, then founded Namo Media (acquired by Twitter in 2014)

founders.name: Einar Vollset
founders.background_notes: YC page: later Managing Partner at Discretion Capital and General Partner at TinySeed

competitors.name: Apple iPhone Mail with Spotlight search
competitors.what: Built in iPhone Mail; iPhone 3.0 added Spotlight search but only over message headers

technical_complexity.rationale: Compressed local copy of the mailbox with a fast full text index on a phone, reported to fit 100,000 messages in 500 MB; hard parts were mobile storage and indexing.

defensibility.rationale: Apple or Google could add full body search in the OS or Gmail app, which is a feature rather than a company.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google bought reMail in February 2010 and pulled the iPhone app from the App Store; the code was later open sourced.

market_need_then: iPhone users had large mailboxes and no body search in Mail in early 2009; Rackspace endorsed reMail in December 2009 for its iPhone customers.

branding.community_and_virality: Press attention when Google bought and removed the app, with headlines about buying then killing it

brand_strength.rationale: Clear and descriptive name with solid launch press, but a simple name for an app that was short lived.

outcome_analysis: reMail built fast full text email search for the iPhone and launched in 2009 while the built in Mail app only searched headers. Google bought the company in February 2010, discontinued the iPhone app and brought the founder Gabor Cselle onto Gmail mobile work, which fits an acquihire; the price was not disclosed in sources seen.
notes: CB Insights lists about 20K from YC and Google as investor (aggregator, unverified, not recorded as a round). Launch date conflicts between TechCrunch May 2009 and later August coverage. remail.com returned HTTP 503. Education of founders not found. Price not found. Completeness pass: the one recorded round rests on a single database (CB Insights, about $20K total over 2 rounds, undated; Google's entry is described as part of the acquisition). Individual round amounts and dates unknown.
